newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria blasts Amnesty International over report.
newsitem.headline: Algeria blasts Amnesty International over report.

text.p: Algeria said on Wednesday that a report by human rights group Amnesty International on widescale abuses in the north African country group was unfair.

"The bias of this organisation is known since a long time. In fact, every year it blacklists the Algerian authorities in a vain attempt aimed at making every interpretation (of the situation) difficult, or perhaps even impossible", the official news agency APS said in a commentary.

Referring to the five-year-old civil strife pitting Moslem guerrillas against the government, it added: "Amnesty International persists in its position of equating law enforcement forces with terrorist groups, whom it sees as an armed opposition... ."

An Amnesty statement on Tuesday quoted secretary-general Pierre Sane as saying that "an atmosphere of terror and lawlessness" ruled in Algeria, where about 60,000 people have died since authorities cancelled a 1992 election which Moslem fundamentalists looked set to win.

APS said the authors of the Amnesty report should have visited the mountainous village of Sidi el Kebir, near Algiers, as well as other locations, where children, women, elderly men and other non-combatants were slaughtered by Moslem guerrillas.

"For pity's sake, wake up! Algeria cannot and will not be for ever what you would want it to be, a country where society's outworn patterns are tested out," it said, alluding to allowing militants to establish a Moslem fundamentalist state.
